os-3-29.alt: A cell drawn in outline. Inside the nucleus, a gene on the DNA is copied into an mRNA molecule. The mRNA leaves the nucleus, and in the cytoplasm a ribosome and tRNA molecules read it to build a protein.

os-3-26.alt: RNA polymerase sitting on a partly unwound stretch of DNA. It moves along the template strand, and a growing RNA strand with bases complementary to the template trails out behind it.

os-3-27.alt: Three steps of splicing. A first RNA copy of a gene contains coding segments (exons) separated by noncoding segments (introns). A spliceosome gathers an intron into a loop, then cuts it out and joins the neighboring exons.

os-3-28.alt: Three panels of translation. The small and large ribosome subunits come together on an mRNA. A tRNA whose anticodon matches the mRNA codon brings its amino acid into the ribosome. In the last panel a growing chain of amino acids leaves the ribosome.

os-3-35.alt: Transcription factor proteins bind to the DNA just ahead of a gene. RNA polymerase then binds alongside them and begins copying the gene.
